extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and legal professionals working with JPO trial and appeal processes
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed procedural and substantive standards governing trial and appeal processes before the Trial and Appeal Department (TAD) of the Japan Patent Office, including appeals, oppositions, trials for invalidation and correction, and Hantei advisory opinions. Useful for practitioners advising clients or conducting proceedings before the JPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality check on filing requests
rubrics_metrics.description: When demandants file a request for a trial or an appeal with the TAD of the JPO, trial clerks will first conduct a formality check to assess, for example, whether the purpose of and reason for the request is stated, whether the fees have been paid and whether the necessary documents, such as a power of attorney, are attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After completing a formality check, trial clerks send the requested cases to the specialized TAD board in charge of the proceedings. Ensure submissions clearly state purpose/reasons, include required fees, and attach necessary documents (e.g., power of attorney) to avoid dismissal at formality stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition and ex officio authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals and trials are conducted by a panel consisting of three or five administrative patent judges. Ex officio proceedings allow a panel to investigate facts and examine evidence on its own authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared that panels may act beyond parties' pleadings by conducting ex officio examinations; anticipate possible panel-led inquiries and the need to address issues the panel raises even if not initially pleaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Manual for Proceedings and Examination Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative patent judges conduct trial and appeal proceedings in accordance with the procedures set out in the Manual for Proceedings, as well as the Examination Guidelines, court decisions and other trial and appeal decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Manual aims to ensure uniform interpretation, consistent and transparent procedures, and fair and accurate decisions. Refer to the Manual and Examination Guidelines when preparing submissions or assessing likely procedural outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence submission requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may submit evidence to the JPO up until the conclusion of a trial or appeal process. Where there is evidence, the parties must state the means of proof in a written request for trial or appeal or a written reply and attach the evidence. When submitting a document prepared in a foreign language, the parties must attach a translation of the text of the part to be examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary evidence typically includes patent gazettes, books, journals, catalogs, blueprints, order forms, delivery slips. Witness examination is possible in invalidation trials; expert opinion and inspections can be obtained applying civil procedure rules. Panels may preserve evidence in advance if later use would be difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction principles
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel must specify the claimed invention based on the description of the claims. The panel construes the claims by referring to the description, drawings and common general knowledge in the technical field of the claimed invention at the time of filing. Even if the invention specified in the description of the claims and the invention described in the description or drawings do not correspond, the panel must not specify the claimed invention based only on the latter: the matters described in the claims must always be taken into consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary source for claim scope is the claim text; use description and drawings and common general knowledge only to interpret claims, not to introduce new subject-matter contrary to claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal against an examiner’s decision of refusal (timing and nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with a JPO examiner’s decision of refusal may file a request for appeal within three months (four months for a party residing outside Japan) from service of the certified copy of the examiner’s decision. It is an ex parte appeal conducted by a panel of administrative patent judges as documentary proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to file within prescribed period due to uncontrollable reasons, an appeal may be filed within 14 days (or two months for overseas residents) after reasons cease but no later than six months after period end. If panel finds the decision inappropriate it may conduct ex officio investigation. If affirmed, appellant may file action with IP High Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to grant — eligibility and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file an opposition to the grant of a patent with the JPO; oppositions do not require any 'interest' on the part of the demandant, but anonymous oppositions are not possible. An opposition must be filed no later than six months from the publication of a gazette containing the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition may be filed claim-by-claim if patent has multiple claims. Prepare to submit reasons and evidence within six-month window after gazette publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition — grounds and scope of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition to the grant of a patent may be made on a number of grounds, including that the patent claims an invention that falls under prior art within Japan or a foreign country at the time of the patent application's filing. A panel will examine only the claims to which an opposition is filed and will conduct the examination on the basis of the reasons and evidence pleaded by the demandant; however, the panel may examine reasons not pleaded in ex officio proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel’s invocation of ex officio examination must consider public interest, purpose of process, delays, and possible accurate determination. If grounds established, panel must rule patent revoked; revocation has retroactive effect (patent deemed never to have existed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition — patentee rights and correction opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: If a panel intends to render a revocation decision, the judge must notify the patentee and any intervenors of the grounds and provide them an opportunity to submit a written opinion within a reasonable specified period. The patentee may file a request for correction of the description, claims or drawings only within this period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee should be ready to submit correction requests promptly when notified of intention to revoke; corrections can be used defensively to preserve patent validity but are time-limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial for correction — purpose and allowed corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may file a request for a trial for correction to correct the claims, description or drawings of the patent. Article 126(1) provides that corrections may be limited to: restriction of the claims, correction of errors or mistranslations, clarification of any ambiguous statement, or rewriting a claim that cites the preceding claim so that it does not cite the preceding claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trials for correction are ex parte documentary proceedings. Corrections are usually preventive to guard against invalidation or to clarify ambiguous parts. A request for correction may not be filed during certain pending proceedings (with some prescribed exceptions) and may not be filed after revocation. If request does not correspond to permitted purposes, chief judge notifies patentee and allows submission of a written opinion; failure may lead to disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on amendments in correction requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the purpose of the request described in a written request for trial has been amended in response to the notice of reasons for rejecting a request for correction, and the gist of the written request has not been changed by the amendment, the amended purpose will be further examined. Where the gist has changed, the amendment will not be adopted and a trial decision will be made by issuing a notice of the conclusion of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid amendments that change the gist of the original request; substantive changes will be refused and explained in the decision reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of allowed corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: If a decision is made to allow a correction (either as a result of a trial or a request for correction) and that decision has become final and binding, the following are deemed to have been made based on the corrected claims, descriptions or drawings with retroactive effect: the filing and publication of the patent application; the examiner’s decision or a trial or appeal decision to the effect that the patent is to be granted; and the registration of the patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful corrections have retroactive effect; strategize corrections carefully because they can change the effective scope and history of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trials for invalidation — standing and inter partes nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons may file a request for a trial for invalidation if they wish to invalidate a patent; trials for invalidation are inter partes trials involving a demandant (interested person) and demandee (patentee). Only an 'interested person' may file, determined case-by-case (examples: person being sued for infringement, a manufacturer of the same kind of product, persons claiming a legitimate right to obtain a patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess standing carefully; evidence of being sued or commercial overlap may qualify. Trials conducted by panels of three or five administrative patent judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for invalidation (Article 123(1) exhaustive list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for invalidation are limited to the statutory reasons under Article 123(1)(i)–(viii): (i) patent granted on an application with amendment not complying with Article 17-2(3) (amendments must be within original disclosure); (ii) patent granted in violation of Articles 25, 29, 29-2, 32, 38, or 39(1)–(4) (conditions for patentability, enjoyment of rights by foreign nationals, unpatentable inventions, joint applications, prior application issues); (iii) patent granted in violation of a treaty; (iv) patent granted on an application not complying with requirements in Article 36(4)(i) or 36(6) re statements of detailed explanation or claims; (v) matters stated in foreign-language application documents are not within scope of foreign-language documents; (vi) patent granted on application filed by a person without right to grant (except where transfer registered); (vii) after grant, patentee falls into category not permitted enjoyment of patent right or patent comes to violate a treaty; (viii) corrections of description/claims/drawings obtained in violation of provisos to Article 126(1), Article 126(5)–(7) (as applied mutatis mutandis) or provisos to Article 120-5(2) or Article 134-2(1). No other reasons outside statutory provisions constitute grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds are exhaustive — craft invalidation requests strictly within statutory items. For example, include arguments on added matter, violations of patentability (novelty/ inventive step), entitlement, procedural/treaty violations, or improper corrections when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee written reply and request for correction in invalidation trials
rubrics_metrics.description: After a demandant files a request for invalidation, a patentee may submit written replies and file a request for correction to protect their patent rights. Corrections may include restriction of claims and clarification of ambiguous statements. A request for correction must identify purpose, must not add new matter, must not substantially expand or change scope of claims, and must fulfill requirements for independent patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits apply: corrections generally must be filed within the time limit for submitting a written reply (first opportunity) or after chief judge provides advance notice of a trial decision. Corrections that become final affect original registration retroactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on demandant amendments and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Demandants may submit written responses or amend the request, but in principle may not amend the request to change the gist of the reasons (e.g., switching from inventive step to clarity) to avoid unreasonable delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that change gist are allowed only if no risk of unreasonable delay and if amendment is in response to a patentee’s request for correction. Plan pleadings to be complete and avoid late gist-changing amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex officio examination limits in invalidation trials
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel may conduct an ex officio examination of any grounds for invalidation not pleaded by a demandant or of violations of correction requirements, but it cannot examine any claim not claimed by a demandant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If panel conducts ex officio proceedings, it must provide parties a 'notice of reasons for invalidation' or 'notice of reasons for rejecting a request for correction,' allowing formal responses. Parties should monitor for such notices and be ready to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings structure and preparatory notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Trials for invalidation are generally conducted as oral proceedings (in-person or online). Prior to oral proceedings, the panel will send a written 'notice of proceedings matters' that clarifies matters to be alleged and proved, issues in dispute, preliminary view of the panel, and may request technical explanations. Based on this, parties must submit an 'oral proceedings statement brief' in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral proceedings enable efficient presentation of arguments and evidence; however documentary allegations are permitted and parties need not restate written allegations at oral proceedings. Prepare an organized statement brief to avoid omissions and to structure oral arguments logically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice of a trial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel will provide parties and intervenors with advance notice of a trial decision when the panel is ready to make a trial decision following oral proceedings and in cases where a reason for trial is approved or a request for correction is not approved. The advance notice contains the same matters as the final decision, including conclusions, reasons, determination of appropriateness of corrections, and validity of all claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice allows patentee to file a request for correction or amend corrected materials; it was established to avoid 'catch-ball' situations with the IP High Court. The panel will not provide advance notice in certain cases (e.g., patentee opts out, no corrections filed and claims found valid, or all requested corrections approved). If patentee requests correction after advance notice, demandant may respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial decision content and appellate recourse
rubrics_metrics.description: The trial decision includes the issues in dispute and the determination of those issues. The panel will determine all reasons for invalidation (including pleaded reasons and ex officio reasons) and present conclusions and specific reasons. It must also describe reasons for not approving amendments changing the gist of a request. Any person dissatisfied may file an action to revoke the trial decision with the IP High Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must be detailed in reasoning; parties dissatisfied may sue at IP High Court naming the opposing party as defendant (the JPO is not a party in revocation suit). Expect thorough exposition of factual and legal determinations in the written decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hantei (infringement advisory opinion) system — nature and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Hantei, a party may request the TAD to deliver and publish an official advisory opinion with respect to the technical scope of a patented invention. An advisory opinion has no legally binding force and no legal interest is required for requesting it, though a benefit in obtaining it must be shown. A written request is served to the demandee who may file a written answer. Hantei examines the technical scope (including doctrine of equivalents) but will not consider indirect infringement under Article 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hantei is an administrative, non-appealable service useful for clarifying scope (e.g., for license negotiations). For standard-essential patents, the requester must identify a 'virtual object' from a technical standard; a three-judge panel compares the patented invention and virtual object to assess essentiality. Use Hantei to gain authoritative but non-binding clarity on scope and equivalents.
